title: Carlo Ancelotti signs Brazil contract extension until 2030 World Cup
content:
Carlo Ancelotti has signed a new four-year contract as the Brazil men’s head coach.

Ancelotti’s new deal, which The Athletic reported in February, will run until the end of the next World Cup in 2030.

“I arrived in Brazil a year ago,” Ancelotti said in a release from the Brazilian Football Federation (CBF). “From the first minute, I understood what football means to this country. For a year, we have been working to bring the Brazilian national team back to the top of the world.

“But the CBF and I want more. More victories, more time, more work. We are very happy to announce that we will continue together for another four years. We will go together until the 2030 World Cup. I want to thank the CBF for their trust. Thank you, Brazil, for the warm welcome and for all the affection.”

Ancelotti joined Brazil in May 2025, with the length of that contract not publicised, ending his second spell as Real Madrid boss and becoming the first foreign head coach of the South American side. The 66-year-old has overseen 10 matches, winning five, drawing two and losing three. He will lead Brazil at the upcoming World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, where they have been drawn in Group C alongside Scotland, Haiti and Morocco.

As well as Madrid, Ancelotti has previously coached clubs including Chelsea, Everton, Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, Napoli and AC Milan. His new contract will also see him lead Brazil at the 2028 Copa America, a competition they last won in 2019.

This deal represents a major win for the Brazilian federation on the eve of World Cup 2026.

Ancelotti was first mooted as a possible Brazil coach when Tite’s spell in charge of the Selecao ended after World Cup 2022. The Italian was not immediately available, however, and later signed a new contract with Real Madrid, leaving Brazil’s federation to cycle through three managers — interim Ramon Menezes, then Fernando Diniz and finally Dorival Junior — in two years.

Eventually, they got their man in May 2025. His impact so far can mostly be felt in the intangibles: a greater sense of calm around the team, growing confidence, the reassurance that comes with having a proven winner in the dugout. Ancelotti’s 10 matches so far have been a mixed bag in terms of results and performances, but there is no doubt that the mood is more positive now than it was when he arrived.

Now, there is certainty about the future, too: whatever happens in June and July, Ancelotti will be around to guide Brazil through the next World Cup cycle. He will be 70 by the time the 2030 tournament comes around; this may not be his last job, but it is starting to feel like his last big swing, a chance to put the finishing touches on what is already a shimmering CV. If he can do that, this summer or in four years’ time, he will be a national hero in Brazil.
